title: Tor & Dark Web Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist for secure Tor usage and dark web browsing. Learn essential privacy hardening steps for anonymous browsing and online safety.
intro: Using Tor and accessing the dark web requires careful preparation to maintain anonymity and security. This checklist covers essential hardening steps to protect your privacy while browsing through onion routing networks.

items.task: Download Tor Browser from official source only
items.why: Fake Tor browsers may contain malware or backdoors that compromise your anonymity.
items.howTo: Visit torproject.org directly, verify the download signature, and never use third-party download sites or app stores.

items.task: Verify Tor Browser's cryptographic signature
items.why: Signature verification ensures you have an authentic, unmodified version of Tor Browser.
items.howTo: Download the signature file from Tor Project website and use GPG to verify the browser package matches the official signature.

items.task: Set Tor Browser security level to 'Safest'
items.why: JavaScript can reveal your real IP address and system information through various exploits.
items.howTo: Click the shield icon in Tor Browser, select 'Advanced Security Settings', and choose 'Safest' level to disable JavaScript.

items.task: Configure bridge relays if in censored regions
items.why: Bridges help bypass ISP blocking and hide the fact that you're using Tor from network monitors.
items.howTo: In Tor Browser settings, go to Connection tab, check 'Use a bridge', and request bridges from torproject.org or use built-in options.

items.task: Ensure all plugins and extensions are disabled
items.why: Browser plugins can leak your real IP address and compromise anonymity through various tracking methods.
items.howTo: Go to about:addons in Tor Browser and verify no extensions are installed. Avoid installing any additional plugins or extensions.

items.task: Use Tor Browser in maximized window only
items.why: Unique window sizes can be used as a fingerprinting technique to track users across sessions.
items.howTo: Always maximize Tor Browser window or use the standard sizes suggested by the browser's resize warning.

items.task: Use a dedicated OS like Tails or Whonix
items.why: Dedicated privacy operating systems provide additional layers of anonymity and prevent IP leaks from other applications.
items.howTo: Boot from Tails live USB for temporary sessions or install Whonix virtual machines for persistent secure environment.

items.task: Disable system-wide Tor if running separate instance
items.why: Multiple Tor instances can interfere with each other and potentially create security vulnerabilities.
items.howTo: Check if Tor daemon is running system-wide with 'systemctl status tor' and disable it if you're using Tor Browser.

items.task: Configure firewall to block non-Tor traffic
items.why: A properly configured firewall prevents accidental IP leaks from other applications while using Tor.
items.howTo: Set up iptables or ufw rules to only allow traffic through Tor ports (9050, 9051) and block all other outbound connections.

items.task: Configure DNS to prevent leaks
items.why: DNS queries outside Tor network can reveal your browsing activity and real location to ISPs or DNS providers.
items.howTo: Set DNS servers to 127.0.0.1 or use a DNS leak-proof configuration in your network settings.

items.task: Disable IPv6 on your system
items.why: IPv6 connections might bypass Tor routing and leak your real IP address to websites and services.
items.howTo: Disable IPv6 in network settings or add 'net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1' to /etc/sysctl.conf on Linux systems.

items.task: Secure system time synchronization
items.why: Accurate timestamps can be used to correlate your activities across different sessions and compromise anonymity.
items.howTo: Use secure NTP servers or disable automatic time sync. Consider using random time offsets for additional protection.

items.task: Always verify .onion site addresses from trusted sources
items.why: Phishing sites with similar .onion addresses can steal credentials or infect your system with malware.
items.howTo: Use verified directories like DarkNetLive or bookmark legitimate sites. Double-check addresses character by character before visiting.

items.task: Never download files through Tor Browser
items.why: Downloaded files can contain malware or tracking beacons that compromise your anonymity when opened.
items.howTo: Avoid downloading any files. If absolutely necessary, scan files offline and open only in isolated environments like virtual machines.

items.task: Never enter personal information or login credentials
items.why: Using real credentials defeats the purpose of anonymous browsing and can link your Tor activity to your identity.
items.howTo: Create separate identities for dark web use. Never log into personal accounts or enter real names, addresses, or payment information.

items.task: Use 'New Identity' feature regularly
items.why: Changing circuits prevents long-term tracking and correlation of your browsing activities across different sites.
items.howTo: Click the onion icon in Tor Browser and select 'New Identity' every 10-15 minutes or when switching to different types of sites.

items.task: Don't mix dark web and regular browsing
items.why: Visiting regular websites through Tor can create patterns that help identify your dark web activities.
items.howTo: Use separate browsers for regular internet and Tor browsing. Consider Incognito Browser for regular private browsing needs.

items.task: Be aware of exit node risks for clearnet sites
items.why: Malicious exit nodes can monitor or modify unencrypted traffic when accessing regular websites through Tor.
items.howTo: Only visit HTTPS sites when browsing clearnet through Tor. Avoid sensitive activities and consider using VPN over Tor for clearnet access.

items.task: Exercise extreme caution on dark web marketplaces
items.why: Many marketplaces are scams, law enforcement honeypots, or contain illegal content that could result in legal consequences.
items.howTo: Research marketplace reputation thoroughly, use escrow services, and be aware of legal risks. Avoid illegal activities entirely.

items.task: Consider VPN over Tor for additional protection
items.why: Adding VPN layer after Tor can hide your traffic from potentially malicious exit nodes.
items.howTo: Connect to a no-logs VPN service after establishing Tor connection. Choose VPN providers that accept cryptocurrency payments.

items.task: Use privacy-focused cryptocurrencies for transactions
items.why: Bitcoin transactions are traceable on the blockchain and can be linked back to your identity through exchange records.
items.howTo: Use Monero or Zcash for private transactions. If using Bitcoin, employ mixing services and create new addresses for each transaction.

items.task: Use encrypted communication tools
items.why: Standard messaging and email services can be monitored and compromise your privacy even when using Tor.
items.howTo: Use Signal, Briar, or Ricochet for messaging. For email, use ProtonMail or Tutanota accessed only through Tor.

items.task: Secure any persistent data storage
items.why: Stored data can be recovered by forensic analysis even after deletion, potentially revealing your activities.
items.howTo: Use full disk encryption, secure deletion tools like shred, or better yet, use amnesic systems like Tails that leave no traces.

items.task: Implement physical security measures
items.why: Physical access to your device can compromise all digital security measures and reveal your Tor usage patterns.
items.howTo: Use full disk encryption, set up secure boot, enable screen locks, and consider using dedicated hardware for Tor activities only.

pro_tips: Test your Tor setup regularly by visiting check.torproject.org to ensure your IP is properly masked and your browser is configured correctly.
Keep Tor Browser updated but wait a few days after new releases to avoid being part of a small, easily identifiable group of early adopters.
Use different exit countries for different activities to avoid patterns, but be aware that some countries have more trustworthy exit nodes than others.
Create a threat model before using Tor - understand what you're protecting against and adjust your security measures accordingly.
Practice good operational security (OPSEC) by maintaining consistent behavior patterns and never mixing your anonymous and real identities online.
